title: GA/237/2002 of STATE Vs SURESH and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
 Government Appeal No. 237 of 2002
State of Uttaranchal .......... Appellant
 versus
Suresh and others .......... Opposite parties

Mr. M.A.Khan, learned AGA, present for the State/Appellant.
Mr. J.S.Panwar, learned Amicus Curiae, present for the respondents.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
 PW 2 Manglanand lodged the first information
report against Suresh and mother of Suresh, Guru Prasad
and Shoula, on 27.01.2001, at 6:10 p.m., in PS Chamba,
Tehri Garhwal, which was registered as case crime no. 30
of 2001, for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A
,304-B IPC and Section 3⁄4 Dowry Prohibition Act. The
incident was alleged to have taken place on 22.01.2001. The
distance between the place of occurrence and the PS
concerned was 13 kilometers. After the investigation, a
charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections
498-A, 304-B IPC and Section 3⁄4 Dowry Prohibition Act
was submitted against Suresh, Guru Prasad, Smt. Shoula
Devi and Smt. Bisla Devi. When the trial began and
prosecution opened it's case, charge for the offences

2
punishable under Sections 498-A, and 304B IPC were
framed on 5th July, 2001. The accused persons pleaded not
guilty and claimed trial.
2. PW 1 Sita Devi (mother of the victim), PW 2
Manglanand (informant, father of the victim), PW 3 Bali
Ram, PW 4 Murlidhar Petwal, PW 5 Head Constable Shri
Chand Singh, PW 6 Head Constable Lalita Prasad, PW 7
Purshottam Prasad Bahuguna, PW 8 Dr. Manoj Badoni and
PW 9 Harpal Singh were examined on behalf of the
prosecution. Incriminating evidence was put to the persons,
in reply to which they said that they have been falsely
implicated in the case. DW 1 Prem Dutt was examined in
defence. After considering the evidence on record, all the
accused were exonerated of the charges levelled against
them, vide judgment and order dated 20.03.2002.
Aggrieved against the impugned order, present Government
Appeal was preferred by the State.
3. The marriage of victim with accused Suresh was
solemnized on 18th November, 1999 and the victim died on
22.01.2001, within one year and three months of the
marriage. The postmortem report indicated that the cause of
death of the victim was asphyxia, as a result of hanging. It
is thus established that Sarita (victim) died within seven
years of her marriage, otherwise than in normal
circumstances. Two limbs of 'dowry death' were therefore
established. In order to prove the dowry death, the
prosecution is required to show that soon before her death,

3
she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband
or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with any
demand for dowry. If the 3rd limb is also proved, then such
death shall be called 'dowry death' and such husband or
relative shall be deemed to have caused her death, as per
Section 304-B IPC.
4. Section 113-B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872,
provides that when the question is whether a person has
committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that
soon before her death, such woman has been subjected by
such person to cruelty, or harassment, for or in connection
with any demand for dowry, the Court shall presume that
such person had caused the 'dowry death'.
5. Prosecution led the evidence through PW 1 and
PW 2. PW 1 was the mother of the deceased. She said, in
her examination-in-chief, that she gifted ornaments in the
marriage of her daughter. She also presented various
articles in her marriage. Her daughter came to her parental
home after a month of her marriage. She said that her
husband, mother-in-law, sister-in-law and brother-in-law
demanded Rs. 50,000/-. Her husband Suresh told to bring
Rs. 50,000/- as he was to establish a business. The victim
replied that her father was a daily wager, from where would
he earn Rs. 50,000/-? PW 1 went to the matrimonial home
of her daughter. Her condition was precarious. She told to
her mother that her mother-in-law assaulted her. Five days
before the death of the victim, she (victim) made a phone

4
call to PW 1 saying that her father, must sent Rs. 50,000/-
immediately. PW 1 replied that her father will be coming by
15th or 16th day of the month, but the victim was done away
with before that. In the cross-examination, PW 1 said that
the accused persons did not demand any dowry at the time
of victim's marriage. The articles given by PW 1 and PW 2
were given as per their own wish. PW 1 was asked various
questions confronting her statement under Section 161
Cr.P.C. She admitted that the victim disclosed to PW 1 only
that the accused persons demanded Rs. 50,000/-. PW 2 was
not present when the victim said so. It is clear from the
cross-examination of PW 1 that she did not highlight many
a things in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., which
she highlighted before the trial court for the first time.
6. PW 2 Manglanand (informant and father of
victim), said that his daughter was married to Suresh Belwal
on 18th November, 1999. His daughter died on 23rd January,
2001. On receiving the news of death of his daughter, PW 2
went to the matrimonial home of the victim. The inquest
report was prepared. He informed to police orally. Written
complaint was given by him on 27th January, 2001. PW 2
proved his complaint (Ext. Ka-1). PW 2 also said that his
daughter came to her parental home after twenty days of her
marriage and complained that Guru Prasad, Guru Prasad's
wife, her mother-in-law Bisla and Suresh harassed her for
non-fulfillment of dowry. The victim also complained to
PW 2 on telephone that they demanded Rs. 50,000/-. Before

5
her death also, she said that the accused persons harassed
her for not bringing Rs. 50,000/-. In the cross-examination,
PW 2 said that the victim was married at the age of 21
years. He also admitted in the cross-examination that no
demand for dowry was made by the accused persons at the
time of marriage. The marriage was solemnized without
turbulence. PW 2 was also informed by Guru Prasad and
others about the death of victim. PW 1 and PW 2 were not
present at their home. PW 2 went to the matrimonial home
of the victim. The police prepared the inquest report. PW 2
did not make a complaint to the police either orally or in
writing regarding the harassment to the victim. He could not
see the dead body of the victim, as the same was sealed by
the police by then. His statement under Section 161 Cr.PC.
was also confronted in his cross-examination, but he could
not explain as to why so many facts, which were
conspicuous by their absence in his statement under Section
161 Cr.P.C., were being said in the Court for the first time.
He also admitted that his daughter did not specify the date
and month when she was harassed by her in-laws. He also
did not indicate in his complaint that a sum of Rs. 50,000/-
was demanded by the victim's in-laws. The only allegation
in the first information report was that the victim was done
away with by her in-laws for want of bringing sufficient
dowry. No panchayat was convened by him on receiving
the complaint of dowry. He admitted in the cross-examination that he gave Rs. 200/- and Rs. 400/- to his
daughter. At internal page no. 13 of his cross-examination,

6
PW 2 also admitted that his son-in-law and daughter were
residing separately from other accused persons. The couple
was residing in different storey and others were living in
different stories. PW 2 was not aware whether or not the
victim committed suicide because victim's husband was
having illicit relations with her bhabhi.
7. PW 3 Bali Ram went to the matrimonial home
of the victim and found that the police sealed her grand
daughter's dead body. PW 4 Murlidhar Petwal also went to
the matrimonial home of the victim, but could not see her
because the police had sealed her dead body by then. PW 5
Head Constable Shri Chand Singh and PW 6 Head
Constable Lalita Prasad were formal witnesses. PW 7
Purshottam Prasad Bahuguna, SI, proved prosecution
papers including inquest report. PW 8 Doctor Manoj
Badoni conducted postmortem on the dead body of the
deceased and opined that cause of her death was asphyxia
as a result of hanging. There were contusion, linear abrasion
and ligature mark ( on the upper side of neck above thyroid
cartilage). PW 9 SI Harpal Singh was the first investigating
officer of the case. DW 1 Prem Dutt said that three different
couples were living separately. In other words, the victim
and her husband were residing separately from other
couples.
8. The 3rd limb of 'dowry death' was therefore, not
proved. PW 1 and PW 2 could not establish that the victim
was subjected to cruelty or harassment for want of bringing

7
sufficient dowry soon before her death. There were many a
facts in their examination-in-chief and cross-examination,
which they told before the trial court for the first time. No
such allegations were made in their statements under
Section 161 Cr.P.C. Those statements were confronted by
learned defence counsel with PW 1 and PW 2 . No doubt
the victim died within seven years of her marriage under
unnatural circumstances, but the reason of her death was
because of harassment and cruelty meted out to her by her
in-laws for want of bringing sufficient dowry was not
proved. It appears that the victim committed suicide,
because her husband was having illicit relations with his
bhabhi, but neither the same was the prosecution story nor
it was proved on the basis of the facts on record. If learned
defence counsel made a suggestion to PW 2 in respect of
the same, the accused cannot be convicted under Section
306 IPC, in as much as, the 'suggestion' cannot partake the
place of 'proof'.
9. The Court below rightly came to the conclusion
that the charge of 'dowry-death' could not be proved by the
prosecution beyond a shadow of reasonable doubt. No
interference is called for in the impugned judgment.
Government Appeal thus fails and is dismissed.
